title: Feature flag + allowlisting + staged rollout tooling for bounded autoscaling
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
content:
## Context
We are rolling out Dedicated autoscaling with customer-configured min/max bounds and (later) predictive scaling. This change can materially affect spend + latency and must be protected by:
- feature flag(s)
- allowlisting at customer + pool granularity
- staged rollout by region / tier
- explicit rollback strategy
- monitoring gates that can automatically halt rollout when correctness degrades (e.g., any bound violation)

This ticket covers the rollout mechanisms/tooling, not the bounds algorithm itself.

## Goals
1) Enable bounded autoscaling behind a flag with explicit allowlisting.
2) Provide safe staged rollout controls (region-by-region, tier-by-tier) with a default-off posture.
3) Provide a clean rollback path (immediate disable) and an operational “freeze” for emergencies.
4) Add rollout safety checks (preflight + post-deploy gates) using existing SLO/alert signals.

## Non-goals
- Building the predictive forecasting pipeline (ENG-2844).
- Building the Console Scaling History UI (ENG-2847) beyond what is necessary to debug rollout issues.

## Proposed flag model
### Runtime behavior flags (evaluated per pool)
- `dedicated.autoscaling.bounds.enabled` (default: false)
  - When false: autoscaler behaves as before (reactive scaling without enforcing min/max semantics).
  - When true: autoscaler clamps desired replicas within evaluated bounds and emits clamp reasons.

- `dedicated.autoscaling.predictive.enabled` (default: false)
  - Separate from bounds. Predictive should never be implicitly enabled when bounds is enabled.

### Rollout scopes
We need to be able to gate by:
- customer org id
- dedicated pool id
- region
- hardware class (optional; useful for early rollout)

Implementation approach:
- Flag evaluation lives in the control plane policy engine (so data plane stays dumb and deterministic).
- Autoscaler consumes “evaluated config” blob that already includes defaults (cooldowns) + resolved bounds; add flag booleans there.

## Allowlisting
Allowlist granularity: pool-level is required (design partners may have multiple pools).
- allowlist is expressed as `org_id + pool_id` tuples.
- provide a fallback “org-wide allowlist” for rapid enablement when customer has many pools.

Admin interface:
- initial: internal CLI (`rw-admin`) + a control plane endpoint.
- later: Console internal-only panel (follow-up ticket if needed).

## Staged rollout plan
Phased enablement:
1) Dogfood (internal Redwood pools): enable per pool in us-west-2 + eu-central-1.
2) Design partners (2–3): enable org-wide but only in agreed regions.
3) Broader beta: allowlist by tier; limit to one region at a time.

We should support a “rollout batch” concept in tooling (not product surface area): a saved list of pools to enable/disable.

## Rollback strategy
### Fast rollback (preferred)
- Toggle `dedicated.autoscaling.bounds.enabled=false` for affected pool(s) or org(s).
- Verify autoscaler desired/applied replicas return to pre-bounds behavior within 1 control loop interval.

### Emergency freeze
- Introduce an override: `dedicated.autoscaling.freeze=true` per pool.
  - Behavior: autoscaler stops applying changes and holds current replica count (still emits decision logs with `action=NOOP_FROZEN`).
  - This is strictly an ops safety valve to stop oscillations or bad actuation.

### Last-resort mitigation
- Pin replicas via existing “manual replicas” mechanism (documented in runbook), then disable flags.

## Monitoring gates (must-have)
Gates are required both as a preflight check (before enabling for a batch) and as an automated post-enable check.

Required gates:
- Bound violations: MUST remain 0 (SLO: 0%). Any violation = halt + page SRE/infra.
- Oscillation rate: <= threshold (see SRE doc). If exceeded, halt further rollout.
- Scale latency (time-to-capacity): <= threshold p95 for the pool cohort.
- Customer-visible p95 latency regression: stop-the-line threshold (especially for design partners).

Implementation details:
- Leverage `observability-pack` dashboards/alerts (ENG-2846) and reference panels in rollout tool output.
- Rollout tool should query the last N minutes of key metrics and block enablement if already unhealthy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Control plane supports storing and evaluating rollout flags for Dedicated pools.
- [x] Internal allowlist mechanism exists (pool + org scopes) and is auditable.
- [x] Autoscaler consumes evaluated flag state; bounded autoscaling is a no-op unless enabled.
- [x] Rollout tooling supports: enable/disable per pool, enable/disable for a batch, and regional constraints.
- [x] Rollout safety checks: preflight health check + post-enable gate with clear “stop the line” behavior.
- [x] Runbook section updated: how to disable flags, how to freeze, how to validate rollback.

## Implementation notes
- Add new evaluated fields to policy engine output:
  - `flags.bounds_enabled`
  - `flags.predictive_enabled`
  - `flags.freeze_autoscaling`
- Determinism: ensure policy evaluation is purely based on config + allowlist state; no time-dependent logic.
- Auditability: allowlist updates emit an admin audit event with actor + reason.

## Links
- PM/rollout coordination thread (Slack): eng-platform/1706728341
- PR: Feature flag + allowlist for bounded autoscaling: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/21927
- Observability gates (dashboards/alerts): https://github.com/redwood/observability-pack/pull/842
- Runbook (autoscaling anomalies): confluence: eng-sre/runbooks/runbook-dedicated-autoscaling-anomalies

## Rollout checklist (operational)
1) Pick cohort (pools) + region(s)
2) Preflight gates: bound violations=0, oscillation within limits, scale latency healthy
3) Enable bounds flag for 1–2 pools
4) Monitor 30–60 min
5) Expand to next batch
6) If any gate fails: disable flag for cohort; if unstable, freeze first then disable

## Open follow-ups (tracked separately)
- Consider adding an internal Console page to view/edit allowlist state (reduce reliance on CLI)
- Decide whether freeze override should remain internal-only long term
- Confirm we have “rollout batch” concept in runbook and who owns it (SRE vs Release)
comments: 2026-01-09 (Benji Okafor): Drafted flag names; proposing separate bounds vs predictive flags to avoid accidentally enabling forecast behavior. Will route through policy engine evaluation so autoscaler remains deterministic.

2026-01-12 (Sean Gallagher): Strong +1 on ‘freeze’ override, but it must be clearly documented as last resort. Also need explicit gates: any bound violation should page immediately and block rollout expansion.

2026-01-16 (Vanessa Ortiz): Please include region constraint in allowlist; fleet capacity is uneven. We should be able to enable us-west-2 first without accidentally turning it on in us-east-1 where we’re tight on supply.

2026-01-22 (Connor O'Brien): Confirmed with PM that design partners are NorthPeak + HelioSearch. We need the tooling ready before enabling them; target end of month for dogfood, first week Feb for partners.
2026-02-04 (Allison Grant): Metrics/dashboards are in good shape; ensure rollout tool links to the exact panels and uses the same SLI definitions (avoid ‘two sources of truth’).

2026-02-11 (Benji Okafor): PR 21927 merged. Added allowlist config + evaluation output fields + ‘freeze’ override. Next: wire rollout preflight checks to alert queries; coordinating with SRE on thresholds.

2026-02-18 (Connor O'Brien): Marking Done. Rollout tooling is live in rw-admin; SRE approved gating thresholds for beta. Dogfood enabled for 3 internal pools (us-west-2) with no bound violations; proceeding to design partner allowlist next.
